# 📑 Metric T2D-INC-01: Percentage of people with newly diagnosed type 2 diabetes in one year (Incidence)

**0. Priority**
**PRIMARY** — this is the leading measure of *new burden*. It signals prevention needs and is widely used for international comparison.

---

**1. Definition (Official wording)**
International Diabetes Federation (IDF): *The percentage of people in the population who are newly diagnosed with type 2 diabetes within a one-year period.*

---

**2. Plain Language Description**
This shows how many people developed type 2 diabetes for the first time in a year, compared to the number of people who were at risk at the start of that year.

---

**3. Formula**

* **Incidence (%)** = (New T2D cases ÷ Population at risk at start of year) × 100
* **Incidence per 1,000** = (New T2D cases ÷ Population at risk) × 1,000

---

**4. Numerator & Denominator**

* **Numerator:** People with a first-ever diagnosis of type 2 diabetes during the reporting year.
* **Denominator:** All individuals aged 20–79 without diabetes at the start of the year, resident in St Helena.

---

**5. Variables Required**

* Date of diagnosis
* Diabetes type (exclude type 1, gestational, secondary)
* Age, sex
* Vital status
* Population denominator (census/administrative registers)

---

**6. Data Source(s)**

* St Helena Diabetes Registry
* Laboratory system (diagnostic confirmation)
* Census / population estimates

---

**7. Data Quality & Caveats**

* Incomplete capture of new diagnoses will underestimate incidence.
* Type misclassification (esp. young adults) is a risk.
* Migration in/out of population may bias denominators.
* Undiagnosed diabetes is not captured.

---

**8. Methodological Notes for Small Numbers**

**Practical implications**

* Annual incidence estimates may be volatile due to small case counts.
* Always report **absolute counts alongside rates**.
* Prefer **per 1,000 population** rates, not percentages, for readability.
* Suppress single-year estimates if denominator <50; instead report 3-year rolling averages.
* Use wide uncertainty bands and clear messaging: “numbers too small for precise year-to-year comparison.”

**Bayesian estimation (technical)**

* Likelihood: Binomial(n, p), Prior: Jeffreys prior Beta(0.5,0.5).
* Posterior: Beta(0.5+x, 0.5+n−x) → report posterior mean and 95% credible interval (CrI).
* Trend smoothing: hierarchical/random-walk model on logit(p) with partial pooling across years.
* Prior sensitivity: compare Beta(0.5,0.5), Beta(1,1), and weakly informative priors centred on UK/IDF comparators.

---

**9. Disaggregation & Standardisation**

* By age group and sex (no geography for St Helena).
* **Age-standardisation:** Use the **WHO World Standard Population (2000–2025 revision)** for global comparison, and the **2013 European Standard Population (ESP)** when benchmarking against UK data.

---

**10. Importance / Uses**

* Core measure of new onset diabetes.
* Evaluates prevention programmes.
* Supports burden-of-disease and cost projections.

---

**11. Reporting Frequency & Format**

* Annually.
* Present as per 1,000 with 95% CrI.
* Line chart for trend; bar chart for age/sex groups.

---

**12. Interpretation Guidance**

* Rising incidence = either more risk factors or better detection.
* Falling incidence may reflect prevention success *or* under-diagnosis.
* In a population of ~4,500, annual changes may reflect chance variation.

---

**13. Responsible Party**
St Helena Public Health Directorate — NCD team; registry manager ensures quality.

---

**14. Linkages to Other Metrics**

* Prevalence (T2D-PREV-02)
* Age at diagnosis (T2D-AGE-03)
* Glycaemic control targets (T2D-HbA1c metrics)

---

**15. Metadata**

* Code: T2D-INC-01
* Source: IDF
* Version: 1.0
* Date updated: 27 Sept 2025

---

**16. Benchmark / Comparison Reference**

* **UK:** NHS Digital, *National Diabetes Audit* (incidence and new diagnoses).
* **International:** IDF Diabetes Atlas (age-standardised incidence estimates).

---

# 📑 Metric T2D-PREV-02: Diagnosed diabetes (Prevalence)

**0. Priority**
**PRIMARY** — prevalence reflects the *total burden of disease*. It drives service demand and is the single most important metric for workforce and resource planning.

---

**1. Definition (Official wording)**
CDC USDSS: *Percentage of the population with a diagnosis of diabetes at a given point in time.*

---

**2. Plain Language Description**
Shows how many people are currently living with diabetes compared to the total population.

---

**3. Formula**

* **Prevalence (%)** = (Diagnosed diabetes cases ÷ Total population) × 100

---

**4. Numerator & Denominator**

* **Numerator:** All people alive on the index date with a diagnosis of diabetes (any type).
* **Denominator:** Total resident population.

---

**5. Variables Required**

* Diagnosis status
* Date of diagnosis
* Vital status (alive on index date)
* Population denominator (census/administrative registers)

---

**6. Data Source(s)**

* St Helena Diabetes Registry
* Census / administrative population data

---

**7. Data Quality & Caveats**

* Misses undiagnosed diabetes, which may be substantial.
* Requires an accurate denominator population.
* Misclassification of diabetes type possible.

---

**8. Methodological Notes for Small Numbers**

**Practical implications**

* Annual prevalence estimates are more stable than incidence but still sensitive to denominator shifts in a small island population.
* Always report **absolute counts alongside rates**.
* Prefer **per 1,000 population** for clarity.
* Use **rounded whole numbers**; avoid spurious decimals.
* If denominator <50 (e.g., age/sex subgroup), suppress subgroup prevalence and report pooled estimates instead.
* Use **3–5 year rolling averages** if subgroup trends are needed.

**Bayesian estimation (technical)**

* Likelihood: Binomial(n, p), Prior: Jeffreys prior Beta(0.5,0.5).
* Posterior: Beta(0.5+x, 0.5+n−x) → report posterior mean and 95% credible interval (CrI).
* Optional: hierarchical model for age/sex groups with partial pooling to stabilise estimates.
* Prior sensitivity: compare Beta(0.5,0.5), Beta(1,1), and weakly informative priors centred on UK/IDF comparators.

---

**9. Disaggregation & Standardisation**

* By age group and sex (no geography for St Helena).
* **Age-standardisation:** Use the **WHO World Standard Population (2000–2025 revision)** for global comparison, and the **2013 European Standard Population (ESP)** when benchmarking against UK data.

---

**10. Importance / Uses**

* Primary measure of disease burden.
* Used for planning service capacity, medicines, and workforce.
* Allows benchmarking with global and UK prevalence.

---

**11. Reporting Frequency & Format**

* Annual reporting.
* Expressed as % or per 1,000 population.
* Present with line charts for trend; bar charts for age/sex breakdown.

---

**12. Interpretation Guidance**

* Rising prevalence may reflect true increases, better detection, or both.
* Short-term changes should be interpreted cautiously in small populations.
* Must be read alongside incidence and mortality trends.

---

**13. Responsible Party**
Public Health Directorate, NCD team.

---

**14. Linkages to Other Metrics**

* Incidence (T2D-INC-01)
* Duration (T2D-DUR-04)
* Age at diagnosis (T2D-AGE-03)

---

**15. Metadata**

* Code: T2D-PREV-02
* Source: CDC USDSS
* Version: 1.0
* Date updated: 27 Sept 2025

---

**16. Benchmark / Comparison Reference**

* **UK:** NHS Digital, *National Diabetes Audit* (prevalence by age/sex).
* **International:** IDF Diabetes Atlas (country-level prevalence).

---

# 📑 Metric T2D-AGE-03: Age at diabetes diagnosis (Mean/median)

**0. Priority**
**SECONDARY** — useful for understanding trends in early onset but not a core burden or service metric.

---

**1. Definition (Official wording)**
CDC USDSS: *Mean or median age at which diabetes is first diagnosed.*

---

**2. Plain Language Description**
The typical age when people are first diagnosed with diabetes.

---

**3. Formula**

* **Mean age at diagnosis** = Sum of ages at diagnosis ÷ Number of new cases
* **Median age at diagnosis** = Middle age in the distribution of new diagnoses

---

**4. Numerator & Denominator**

* **Numerator:** Sum (for mean) or distribution (for median) of ages at diagnosis.
* **Denominator:** Number of new cases.

---

**5. Variables Required**

* Date of birth
* Date of diagnosis

---

**6. Data Source(s)**

* Registry records with date of birth and diagnosis date.

---

**7. Data Quality & Caveats**

* Errors in recording dates bias results.
* Small numbers may produce unstable estimates, especially for means.

---

**8. Methodological Notes for Small Numbers**

**Practical implications**

* Report **median age with interquartile range (IQR)**, which is more robust to outliers.
* Aggregate into 3-year blocks if <30 new cases annually.
* Present both **median** and **range or IQR** instead of mean alone.

**Bayesian estimation (technical)**

* For mean: Bayesian t-distribution models with weakly informative priors can stabilise estimates.
* For medians: BCa bootstrap intervals are preferable.
* Small-n sensitivity analysis: compare annual vs pooled multi-year medians.

---

**9. Disaggregation & Standardisation**

* By sex and broad age groups (no geography).
* **Age-standardisation is not applicable** since this is already an age-based measure.

---

**10. Importance / Uses**

* Detects whether diabetes onset is shifting to younger ages.
* Earlier onset implies longer exposure and greater lifetime burden.

---

**11. Reporting Frequency & Format**

* Annually (or 3-year rolling if sparse).
* Present mean and median, with boxplots for distribution.

---

**12. Interpretation Guidance**

* A falling age at diagnosis indicates earlier onset.
* Must be interpreted carefully in small populations where a few young cases can shift averages.

---

**13. Responsible Party**
Registry team (Public Health Directorate).

---

**14. Linkages to Other Metrics**

* Incidence (T2D-INC-01)
* Duration (T2D-DUR-04)

---

**15. Metadata**

* Code: T2D-AGE-03
* Source: CDC USDSS
* Version: 1.0

---

**16. Benchmark / Comparison Reference**

* **UK:** NHS Digital, *National Diabetes Audit* (age at diagnosis distribution).
* **International:** ICHOM standard set for diabetes outcomes.

---

# 📑 Metric T2D-DUR-04: Duration of diabetes (Mean/median)

**0. Priority**
**SECONDARY** — provides useful context for chronic burden but less central than prevalence or control metrics.

---

**1. Definition (Official wording)**
CDC USDSS: *Mean or median duration of diabetes among diagnosed patients.*

---

**2. Plain Language Description**
Shows how long people have lived with diabetes since their diagnosis.

---

**3. Formula**

* **Mean duration (years)** = Sum of years since diagnosis ÷ Number of people with diabetes
* **Median duration (years)** = Middle value of years since diagnosis among cases

---

**4. Numerator & Denominator**

* **Numerator:** Sum (for mean) or distribution (for median) of years since diagnosis.
* **Denominator:** People alive with a diabetes diagnosis.

---

**5. Variables Required**

* Date of diagnosis
* Current date (or date of death if deceased)

---

**6. Data Source(s)**

* St Helena Diabetes Registry

---

**7. Data Quality & Caveats**

* Missing mortality data will inflate duration.
* In early registry years, mean duration will be underestimated.

---

**8. Methodological Notes for Small Numbers**

**Practical implications**

* Report **median duration** alongside mean.
* Group into bands (<5 years, 5–10 years, >10 years) to reduce volatility.
* Use rolling averages if small n.

**Bayesian estimation (technical)**

* Bayesian survival models could be used to account for censoring.
* Alternatively, model duration distribution with weakly informative priors to estimate median with uncertainty.

---

**9. Disaggregation & Standardisation**

* By age and sex (no geography).
* **Age-standardisation not applicable** (duration is a time-based measure).

---

**10. Importance / Uses**

* Longer duration increases complication risks.
* Rising mean duration may reflect improved survival.

---

**11. Reporting Frequency & Format**

* Annual reporting.
* Present mean/median years; bar charts by duration band.

---

**12. Interpretation Guidance**

* Increasing duration suggests improved survival.
* Shorter duration may suggest poor outcomes or high mortality.

---

**13. Responsible Party**
Registry manager; NCD epidemiology team.

---

**14. Linkages to Other Metrics**

* Age at diagnosis (T2D-AGE-03)
* Mortality (future indicators)

---

**15. Metadata**

* Code: T2D-DUR-04
* Source: CDC USDSS
* Version: 1.0

---

**16. Benchmark / Comparison Reference**

* **UK:** NHS Digital, *National Diabetes Audit* (duration distribution).
* **International:** WHO/IDF registry comparisons.

---

# 📑 Metric T2D-PREG-05: Diabetes in pregnancy (Prevalence)

**0. Priority**
**SECONDARY** — numbers will be very small in St Helena, but important for maternal and child health surveillance.

---

**1. Definition (Official wording)**
CDC USDSS: *Prevalence of diabetes (any type) during pregnancy.*

---

**2. Plain Language Description**
Shows how many pregnant women already have diabetes during pregnancy.

---

**3. Formula**

* **Prevalence (%)** = (Pregnant women with diabetes ÷ Total pregnancies) × 100

---

**4. Numerator & Denominator**

* **Numerator:** Pregnant women diagnosed with diabetes.
* **Denominator:** All pregnancies in the reporting period.

---

**5. Variables Required**

* Pregnancy status
* Diabetes diagnosis and type

---

**6. Data Source(s)**

* St Helena Diabetes Registry
* Maternity records

---

**7. Data Quality & Caveats**

* Requires distinction between pre-existing and gestational diabetes.
* Very small numbers lead to high volatility.

---

**8. Methodological Notes for Small Numbers**

**Practical implications**

* Always report **absolute numbers** alongside %.
* Use **3–5 year pooling** for stable estimates.
* Suppress annual % if denominator <50 pregnancies.

**Bayesian estimation (technical)**

* Likelihood: Binomial(n, p), Prior: Jeffreys prior Beta(0.5,0.5).
* Posterior: Beta(0.5+x, 0.5+n−x).
* Multi-year hierarchical models can stabilise very small denominators.

---

**9. Disaggregation & Standardisation**

* By maternal age only (no geography).
* **Age-standardisation:** If needed, use WHO World Standard Population or 2013 ESP for comparison, though small N may limit feasibility.

---

**10. Importance / Uses**

* Important for maternal and fetal outcomes.
* Informs antenatal care planning.

---

**11. Reporting Frequency & Format**

* Annual, but pooled multi-year reporting recommended.
* Report both % and absolute numbers.

---

**12. Interpretation Guidance**

* High prevalence may reflect high background diabetes burden.
* Year-to-year changes should not be over-interpreted.

---

**13. Responsible Party**
Maternity services and registry team.

---

**14. Linkages to Other Metrics**

* Gestational diabetes incidence (T2D-GDM-06)
* Pre-pregnancy diabetes (future metrics)

---

**15. Metadata**

* Code: T2D-PREG-05
* Source: CDC USDSS
* Version: 1.0

---

**16. Benchmark / Comparison Reference**

* **UK:** NHS *National Maternity and Perinatal Audit* (diabetes in pregnancy).
* **International:** WHO/IDF maternal diabetes statistics.

---

# 📑 Metric T2D-GDM-06: Gestational diabetes mellitus (Incidence)

**0. Priority**
**SECONDARY** — numbers are very small in St Helena, so this metric is more descriptive than statistical.

---

**1. Definition (Official wording)**
CDC USDSS: *Incidence of gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) in a defined year.*

---

**2. Plain Language Description**
Shows what proportion of pregnancies are affected by gestational diabetes.

---

**3. Formula**

* **Incidence (%)** = (New GDM cases ÷ Total pregnancies in year) × 100

---

**4. Numerator & Denominator**

* **Numerator:** Pregnant women newly diagnosed with GDM during pregnancy.
* **Denominator:** All pregnancies in the reporting year.

---

**5. Variables Required**

* Pregnancy identifier
* Date of GDM diagnosis
* Maternal age, BMI (if available)

---

**6. Data Source(s)**

* Maternity records
* St Helena Diabetes Registry

---

**7. Data Quality & Caveats**

* Screening practices strongly affect incidence.
* Requires exclusion of pre-existing diabetes.
* Small numbers make estimates volatile.

---

**8. Methodological Notes for Small Numbers**

**Practical implications**

* Report **absolute numbers + %** together.
* Use **3–5 year pooled incidence** for trend reporting.
* Suppress single-year estimates if <50 pregnancies.

**Bayesian estimation (technical)**

* Likelihood: Binomial(n, p), Prior: Jeffreys Beta(0.5,0.5).
* Posterior: Beta(0.5+x, 0.5+n−x).
* Consider hierarchical pooling across years for stability.

---

**9. Disaggregation & Standardisation**

* By maternal age or BMI group (no geography).
* **Age-standardisation:** Use WHO World Standard Population or ESP if comparing internationally, though small sample size may limit feasibility.

---

**10. Importance / Uses**

* Key maternal outcome.
* Important for antenatal care, neonatal health, and future maternal risk.

---

**11. Reporting Frequency & Format**

* Annual reporting; recommend pooled multi-year presentation.

---

**12. Interpretation Guidance**

* Rising incidence may reflect obesity, older maternal age, or better screening.

---

**13. Responsible Party**
Maternity and registry teams.

---

**14. Linkages to Other Metrics**

* Diabetes in pregnancy (T2D-PREG-05)
* Pre-pregnancy diabetes (future indicator)

---

**15. Metadata**

* Code: T2D-GDM-06
* Source: CDC USDSS
* Version: 1.0

---

**16. Benchmark / Comparison Reference**

* **UK:** NHS *National Maternity and Perinatal Audit* (gestational diabetes rates).
* **International:** WHO and IDF maternal health indicators.

---

# 📑 Metric T2D-W18-44-07: Diabetes prevalence among women aged 18–44 years

**0. Priority**
**SECONDARY** — important for reproductive health, but numbers are small.

---

**1. Definition (Official wording)**
CDC Chronic Disease Indicators: *Percentage of women aged 18–44 with diabetes.*

---

**2. Plain Language Description**
Shows how common diabetes is among women of childbearing age.

---

**3. Formula**

* **Prevalence (%)** = (Women aged 18–44 with diabetes ÷ All women aged 18–44) × 100

---

**4. Numerator & Denominator**

* **Numerator:** Women aged 18–44 diagnosed with diabetes.
* **Denominator:** All women aged 18–44 in the population.

---

**5. Variables Required**

* Age, sex
* Diagnosis status

---

**6. Data Source(s)**

* Registry
* Census population estimates

---

**7. Data Quality & Caveats**

* May underestimate true prevalence due to undiagnosed cases.
* Age and sex classification must be accurate.

---

**8. Methodological Notes for Small Numbers**

**Practical implications**

* Always report **absolute counts + %**.
* Use **broad age bands** (18–29, 30–44).
* Suppress subgroup estimates if denominator <50.

**Bayesian estimation (technical)**

* Binomial(n, p), Prior: Beta(0.5,0.5).
* Posterior mean + 95% CrI.
* Partial pooling across years can stabilise.

---

**9. Disaggregation & Standardisation**

* Report only by broad maternal age bands (no geography).
* **Age-standardisation:** Not usually needed, as this is already an age-specific measure.

---

**10. Importance / Uses**

* Identifies reproductive-age women at risk.
* Informs pre-conception and antenatal care services.

---

**11. Reporting Frequency & Format**

* Annual; 3-year rolling averages if small N.

---

**12. Interpretation Guidance**

* High prevalence in this group may reflect obesity and other risk factors.

---

**13. Responsible Party**
Registry and reproductive health services.

---

**14. Linkages to Other Metrics**

* Pregnancy-related diabetes (T2D-PREG-05, T2D-GDM-06).

---

**15. Metadata**

* Code: T2D-W18-44-07
* Source: CDC CDI
* Version: 1.0

---

**16. Benchmark / Comparison Reference**

* **UK:** NHS Digital, *Maternity Services Data Set* (diabetes prevalence in younger women).
* **International:** IDF Diabetes Atlas, women’s health tables.

---

# 📑 Metric T2D-TYPE-08: Diabetes type (Prevalence of each type)

**0. Priority**
**SECONDARY** — useful for context, but not a primary planning metric.

---

**1. Definition (Official wording)**
ICHOM: *Proportion of all diagnosed diabetes cases by type (Type 1, Type 2, gestational, other).*

---

**2. Plain Language Description**
Shows the distribution of diabetes types among people with the condition.

---

**3. Formula**

* **Prevalence (%) of type X** = (Cases of type X ÷ All diagnosed diabetes cases) × 100

---

**4. Numerator & Denominator**

* **Numerator:** Cases of a specific type.
* **Denominator:** All diagnosed diabetes cases.

---

**5. Variables Required**

* Diabetes type
* Diagnosis status

---

**6. Data Source(s)**

* Registry diagnosis fields

---

**7. Data Quality & Caveats**

* Misclassification is common.
* Requires consistent diagnostic coding.

---

**8. Methodological Notes for Small Numbers**

**Practical implications**

* Report **absolute counts and %**.
* Combine rare types into “Other.”
* Suppress % if cell count <5.

**Bayesian estimation (technical)**

* Multinomial likelihood, Prior: Dirichlet(0.5,…,0.5).
* Posterior = Dirichlet(0.5+xk).
* Report mean + 95% CrI for each category.

---

**9. Disaggregation & Standardisation**

* By sex and age group (no geography).
* **Age-standardisation:** Use WHO or ESP for comparing type distribution internationally, though often presented as raw proportions.

---

**10. Importance / Uses**

* Helps anticipate treatment needs (insulin vs tablets).
* Monitors epidemiological shifts (e.g., more type 2 at younger ages).

---

**11. Reporting Frequency & Format**

* Annual reporting.
* Use distribution tables or pie charts.

---

**12. Interpretation Guidance**

* Shifts in type mix signal changing population risk profiles.

---

**13. Responsible Party**
Registry management team.

---

**14. Linkages to Other Metrics**

* Incidence (T2D-INC-01)
* Age at diagnosis (T2D-AGE-03)

---

**15. Metadata**

* Code: T2D-TYPE-08
* Source: ICHOM
* Version: 1.0

---

**16. Benchmark / Comparison Reference**

* **UK:** NHS Digital, *National Diabetes Audit* (type distribution).
* **International:** IDF Diabetes Atlas.

---

# 📑 Metric T2D-HBA1c-1x-09: Percentage of people with type 2 diabetes with at least 1 HbA1c measurement in the year

**0. Priority**
**PRIMARY** — this is a key process-of-care metric.

---

**1. Definition (Official wording)**
IDF Clinical Guidelines Task Force (2012): *Percentage of people with type 2 diabetes who had at least one HbA1c measurement in the past year.*

---

**2. Plain Language Description**
Shows whether people with diabetes are getting their recommended annual blood sugar test.

---

**3. Formula**

* **% with ≥1 HbA1c test** = (People with T2D who had ≥1 HbA1c in year ÷ All people with T2D) × 100

---

**4. Numerator & Denominator**

* **Numerator:** People with T2D who had ≥1 HbA1c recorded in the year.
* **Denominator:** All people with T2D in the registry.

---

**5. Variables Required**

* Diabetes type
* HbA1c test date(s)

---

**6. Data Source(s)**

* Registry
* Laboratory information system

---

**7. Data Quality & Caveats**

* Missing lab linkages may underestimate coverage.
* Must exclude duplicate results.

---

**8. Methodological Notes for Small Numbers**

**Practical implications**

* Annual coverage should be reasonably stable, but subgroups may be small.
* Always report **counts and %**.
* Suppress subgroup reporting if denominator <50.

**Bayesian estimation (technical)**

* Binomial(n, p) with Jeffreys prior.
* Posterior mean and 95% CrI.
* Partial pooling across years can smooth trends.

---

**9. Disaggregation & Standardisation**

* By age and sex (no geography).
* **Age-standardisation:** Use WHO World Standard Population for international comparison; ESP for UK benchmarking.

---

**10. Importance / Uses**

* Core indicator of care quality.
* Ensures patients receive minimum monitoring.

---

**11. Reporting Frequency & Format**

* Annual reporting.
* Present % with ≥1 HbA1c, plus complement (none).

---

**12. Interpretation Guidance**

* Low values suggest gaps in monitoring.
* Should be ≥90% in well-functioning systems.

---

**13. Responsible Party**
Registry manager; NCD clinical services.

---

**14. Linkages to Other Metrics**

* Complements Metric 10 (no HbA1c).
* Links to HbA1c control metrics (14–15).

---

**15. Metadata**

* Code: T2D-HBA1c-1x-09
* Source: IDF 2012
* Version: 1.0

---

**16. Benchmark / Comparison Reference**

* **UK:** NHS Digital, *National Diabetes Audit – Care Processes*.
* **International:** IDF guideline standards.

---

# 📑 Metric T2D-HBA1c-None-10: Percentage of people with type 2 diabetes with no HbA1c measurement in the year

**0. Priority**
**SECONDARY** — this is the complement of Metric 9 and rarely needed separately.

---

**1. Definition (Official wording)**
IDF Clinical Guidelines Task Force (2012): *Percentage of people with type 2 diabetes who had no HbA1c measurement in the past year.*

---

**2. Plain Language Description**
Shows whether people with diabetes are missing their recommended annual blood sugar test.

---

**3. Formula**

* **% with no HbA1c test** = (People with T2D who had zero HbA1c tests in year ÷ All people with T2D) × 100
* **Note:** This is 100 – Metric 9.

---

**4. Numerator & Denominator**

* **Numerator:** People with T2D who had zero HbA1c in year.
* **Denominator:** All people with T2D in the registry.

---

**5. Variables Required**

* Diabetes type
* HbA1c test date(s)

---

**6. Data Source(s)**

* Registry
* Laboratory system

---

**7. Data Quality & Caveats**

* May reflect data capture issues rather than true absence of testing.

---

**8. Methodological Notes for Small Numbers**

**Practical implications**

* Derived directly from Metric 9.
* No need to model separately.

**Bayesian estimation (technical)**

* Derived as complement of Metric 9’s posterior distribution.

---

**9. Disaggregation & Standardisation**

* By age and sex (no geography).
* **Age-standardisation:** As per Metric 9.

---

**10. Importance / Uses**

* Secondary indicator.
* Highlights groups missing annual review.

---

**11. Reporting Frequency & Format**

* Annual reporting.
* Report alongside Metric 9.

---

**12. Interpretation Guidance**

* High values indicate monitoring gaps.

---

**13. Responsible Party**
Registry manager; NCD services.

---

**14. Linkages to Other Metrics**

* Direct complement of Metric 9.

---

**15. Metadata**

* Code: T2D-HBA1c-None-10
* Source: IDF 2012
* Version: 1.0

---

**16. Benchmark / Comparison Reference**

* **UK:** NHS Digital, *National Diabetes Audit – Care Processes*.
* **International:** IDF guideline standards.

---

# 📑 Metric T2D-SMBG-11(A-B): Percentage of people (A) All people with T2 diabetes, (B) with insulin-treated diabetes) routinely performing self-monitoring of blood glucose (SMBG)

**0. Priority**
**SECONDARY** — useful for assessing patient engagement, but small denominators in St Helena mean estimates will be unstable.

---

**1. Definition (Official wording)**
IDF Clinical Guidelines Task Force (2012): *Percentage of people with insulin-treated diabetes who routinely perform SMBG.*

---

**2. Plain Language Description**
Shows how many people on insulin are checking their blood sugar regularly at home.

---

**3. Formula**

* **% performing SMBG** = (People on insulin reporting regular SMBG ÷ All insulin-treated people with diabetes) × 100

---

**4. Numerator & Denominator**

* **Numerator:** Insulin-treated people with diabetes who report or have records of SMBG.
* **Denominator:** All insulin-treated people with diabetes in the registry.

---

**5. Variables Required**

* Diabetes type
* Medication status (insulin)
* SMBG status (yes/no, frequency if available)

---

**6. Data Source(s)**

* Registry
* Patient self-report or clinic documentation

---

**7. Data Quality & Caveats**

* Relies on self-report, which may overestimate compliance.
* Very small numbers in St Helena.

---

**8. Methodological Notes for Small Numbers**

**Practical implications**

* Report **counts and %** together.
* Pool data across **3–5 years** to achieve stable rates.
* Suppress if denominator <20.

**Bayesian estimation (technical)**

* Binomial(n, p), Prior: Beta(0.5,0.5).
* Posterior mean and 95% CrI.
* Consider hierarchical modelling if stratifying.

---

**9. Disaggregation & Standardisation**

* By sex and age group (no geography).
* **Age-standardisation:** Optional; WHO/ESP may be used if comparing internationally.

---

**10. Importance / Uses**

* Indicates whether insulin-treated patients are monitoring adequately.
* Supports education and adherence interventions.

---

**11. Reporting Frequency & Format**

* Annual, but pooled reporting recommended.

---

**12. Interpretation Guidance**

* Low levels suggest need for patient education and support.

---

**13. Responsible Party**
Registry team; diabetes nurse specialist.

---

**14. Linkages to Other Metrics**

* Medication use (T2D-MED-21)
* HbA1c control (Metrics 14–15)

---

**15. Metadata**

* Code: T2D-SMBG-11
* Source: IDF 2012
* Version: 1.0

---

**16. Benchmark / Comparison Reference**

* **UK:** NHS NDA (if SMBG reported).
* **International:** IDF Clinical Practice Recommendations.

---

# 📑 Metric T2D-HbA1c≤64-12: Percentage of patients with diabetes whose last HbA1c was ≤64 mmol/mol (8.0%)

**0. Priority**
**SECONDARY** — overlaps with more clinically relevant targets (≤53 mmol/mol, ≥75 mmol/mol).

---

**1. Definition (Official wording)**
NICE QOF: *Percentage of patients with diabetes on the register whose last HbA1c was ≤64 mmol/mol in the past 12 months.*

---

**2. Plain Language Description**
Shows how many patients have good blood sugar control, using an HbA1c cut-off of 8.0%.

---

**3. Formula**

* **% ≤64 mmol/mol** = (Patients with last HbA1c ≤64 mmol/mol ÷ All patients with diabetes) × 100

---

**4. Numerator & Denominator**

* **Numerator:** Patients with last HbA1c ≤64 mmol/mol.
* **Denominator:** All people with diabetes.

---

**5. Variables Required**

* Latest HbA1c result in past year
* Diabetes status

---

**6. Data Source(s)**

* Registry
* Laboratory data

---

**7. Data Quality & Caveats**

* Must use most recent HbA1c only.
* Missing data will bias results.

---

**8. Methodological Notes for Small Numbers**

**Practical implications**

* Always show **counts and %**.
* Suppress subgroup estimates if denominator <50.
* Use rolling averages if needed.

**Bayesian estimation (technical)**

* Binomial likelihood with Jeffreys prior.
* Posterior mean + 95% CrI.
* Possible hierarchical shrinkage across age/sex groups.

---

**9. Disaggregation & Standardisation**

* By age and sex.
* **Age-standardisation:** WHO and ESP if comparing internationally.

---

**10. Importance / Uses**

* Tracks intermediate control threshold.
* Supports QOF and international reporting.

---

**11. Reporting Frequency & Format**

* Annual reporting.

---

**12. Interpretation Guidance**

* High % suggests majority are reasonably controlled.
* Complements stricter (<53) and looser (≤75) thresholds.

---

**13. Responsible Party**
Registry; primary care diabetes services.

---

**14. Linkages to Other Metrics**

* HbA1c <53 mmol/mol (T2D-HbA1c<53-14)
* HbA1c ≥75 mmol/mol (T2D-HbA1c≥75-15)

---

**15. Metadata**

* Code: T2D-HbA1c≤64-12
* Source: NICE QOF
* Version: 1.0

---

**16. Benchmark / Comparison Reference**

* **UK:** NHS QOF indicators.
* **International:** IDF guideline thresholds.

---

# 📑 Metric T2D-HbA1c≤75-13: Percentage of patients with diabetes whose last HbA1c was ≤75 mmol/mol (9.0%)

**0. Priority**
**SECONDARY** — a looser threshold, less clinically meaningful but useful for monitoring worst control.

---

**1. Definition (Official wording)**
NICE QOF: *Percentage of patients with diabetes on the register whose last HbA1c was ≤75 mmol/mol in the past 12 months.*

---

**2. Plain Language Description**
Shows how many patients are avoiding very poor control (above 9.0%).

---

**3. Formula**

* **% ≤75 mmol/mol** = (Patients with last HbA1c ≤75 ÷ All patients with diabetes) × 100

---

**4. Numerator & Denominator**

* **Numerator:** Patients with last HbA1c ≤75 mmol/mol.
* **Denominator:** All people with diabetes.

---

**5. Variables Required**

* Latest HbA1c result in past year
* Diabetes status

---

**6. Data Source(s)**

* Registry
* Laboratory data

---

**7. Data Quality & Caveats**

* Missing lab results reduce denominator coverage.
* Data completeness essential.

---

**8. Methodological Notes for Small Numbers**

**Practical implications**

* Report as context to other HbA1c thresholds.
* Suppress subgroup estimates if denominator <50.

**Bayesian estimation (technical)**

* Binomial(n, p), Beta(0.5,0.5).
* Posterior mean and 95% CrI.

---

**9. Disaggregation & Standardisation**

* By age and sex.
* **Age-standardisation:** WHO and ESP if international comparisons needed.

---

**10. Importance / Uses**

* Indicates how many patients are keeping below very high HbA1c levels.
* Complements stricter thresholds.

---

**11. Reporting Frequency & Format**

* Annual reporting.

---

**12. Interpretation Guidance**

* High % suggests most patients avoid worst control.

---

**13. Responsible Party**
Registry; clinical services.

---

**14. Linkages to Other Metrics**

* HbA1c <53 mmol/mol (T2D-HbA1c<53-14)
* HbA1c ≥75 mmol/mol (T2D-HbA1c≥75-15)

---

**15. Metadata**

* Code: T2D-HbA1c≤75-13
* Source: NICE QOF
* Version: 1.0

---

**16. Benchmark / Comparison Reference**

* **UK:** NHS QOF indicators.
* **International:** IDF guideline thresholds.

# 📑 Metric T2D-HbA1c<53-14: Percentage of people with type 2 diabetes with HbA1c <53 mmol/mol (7.0%)

**0. Priority**
**PRIMARY** — the most clinically relevant threshold for good glycaemic control.

---

**1. Definition (Official wording)**
IDF Clinical Guidelines Task Force: *Percentage of people with type 2 diabetes whose HbA1c is <53 mmol/mol (7.0%).*

---

**2. Plain Language Description**
Shows the proportion of patients meeting the standard target for good blood sugar control.

---

**3. Formula**

* **% <53 mmol/mol** = (Patients with HbA1c <53 mmol/mol ÷ All people with type 2 diabetes) × 100

---

**4. Numerator & Denominator**

* **Numerator:** People with T2D and last HbA1c <53 mmol/mol.
* **Denominator:** All people with T2D in registry.

---

**5. Variables Required**

* Latest HbA1c result
* Diabetes type

---

**6. Data Source(s)**

* Registry
* Laboratory system

---

**7. Data Quality & Caveats**

* Missing HbA1c results reduce denominator completeness.
* Must use most recent result only.

---

**8. Methodological Notes for Small Numbers**

**Practical implications**

* Report **counts and %**.
* Suppress subgroup reporting if denominator <50.
* Show rolling averages for subgroups.

**Bayesian estimation (technical)**

* Binomial likelihood with Jeffreys prior.
* Posterior mean + 95% CrI.
* Consider hierarchical shrinkage across age/sex groups.

---

**9. Disaggregation & Standardisation**

* By age and sex.
* **Age-standardisation:** WHO World Standard Population and 2013 ESP for comparisons.

---

**10. Importance / Uses**

* Internationally recognised treatment target.
* Indicator of effective management and reduced risk of complications.

---

**11. Reporting Frequency & Format**

* Annual.

---

**12. Interpretation Guidance**

* High % indicates good glycaemic management.

---

**13. Responsible Party**
Registry; diabetes specialist nurse.

---

**14. Linkages to Other Metrics**

* HbA1c ≥75 mmol/mol (T2D-HbA1c≥75-15)
* Care process metrics (T2D-HBA1c-1x-09)

---

**15. Metadata**

* Code: T2D-HbA1c<53-14
* Source: IDF 2012
* Version: 1.0

---

**16. Benchmark / Comparison Reference**

* **UK:** NHS NDA (HbA1c <7% target).
* **International:** IDF Diabetes Atlas (control indicators).

---

# 📑 Metric T2D-HbA1c≥75-15: Percentage of people with type 2 diabetes with HbA1c ≥75 mmol/mol (9.0%)

**0. Priority**
**PRIMARY** — identifies patients with poor control, at highest risk of complications.

---

**1. Definition (Official wording)**
IDF Clinical Guidelines Task Force: *Percentage of people with type 2 diabetes whose HbA1c is ≥75 mmol/mol (9.0%).*

---

**2. Plain Language Description**
Shows the proportion of patients with very poor blood sugar control.

---

**3. Formula**

* **% ≥75 mmol/mol** = (Patients with HbA1c ≥75 ÷ All people with type 2 diabetes) × 100

---

**4. Numerator & Denominator**

* **Numerator:** People with T2D and last HbA1c ≥75 mmol/mol.
* **Denominator:** All people with T2D in registry.

---

**5. Variables Required**

* Latest HbA1c result
* Diabetes type

---

**6. Data Source(s)**

* Registry
* Laboratory system

---

**7. Data Quality & Caveats**

* Must use most recent HbA1c only.
* Missing data may underestimate poor control.

---

**8. Methodological Notes for Small Numbers**

**Practical implications**

* Always report **counts + %**.
* Flag absolute numbers since very poor control is rare.
* Suppress subgroup % if denominator <50.

**Bayesian estimation (technical)**

* Binomial(n, p) with Beta(0.5,0.5).
* Posterior mean and 95% CrI.

---

**9. Disaggregation & Standardisation**

* By age and sex.
* **Age-standardisation:** WHO and ESP if comparing internationally.

---

**10. Importance / Uses**

* Identifies high-risk patients who need urgent clinical attention.
* Guides targeted interventions.

---

**11. Reporting Frequency & Format**

* Annual.
* Report alongside HbA1c <53 mmol/mol.

---

**12. Interpretation Guidance**

* Higher % indicates significant clinical management issues.

---

**13. Responsible Party**
Registry; diabetes specialist nurse.

---

**14. Linkages to Other Metrics**

* HbA1c <53 mmol/mol (T2D-HbA1c<53-14)
* Process metrics (T2D-HBA1c-1x-09)

---

**15. Metadata**

* Code: T2D-HbA1c≥75-15
* Source: IDF 2012
* Version: 1.0

---

**16. Benchmark / Comparison Reference**

* **UK:** NHS NDA (HbA1c ≥9% metric).
* **International:** IDF guideline thresholds.

# 📑 Metric T2D-Diet-16: Percentage of patients with diabetes who had a dietary review within the last 15 months

**0. Priority**
**SECONDARY** — a useful quality of care process measure, but not central for burden or risk tracking.

---

**1. Definition (Official wording)**
NICE QOF: *Percentage of patients with diabetes on the register who have had a dietary review by a suitably competent professional in the preceding 15 months.*

---

**2. Plain Language Description**
Shows how many people with diabetes received professional dietary advice or review in the past 15 months.

---

**3. Formula**

* **% with dietary review** = (Patients with record of dietary review ÷ All patients with diabetes) × 100

---

**4. Numerator & Denominator**

* **Numerator:** Patients with documented dietary review in the past 15 months.
* **Denominator:** All patients with diabetes.

---

**5. Variables Required**

* Date of last dietary review
* Diabetes diagnosis status

---

**6. Data Source(s)**

* Registry
* Clinical care records

---

**7. Data Quality & Caveats**

* Relies on consistent recording.
* Quality of advice not measured.

---

**8. Methodological Notes for Small Numbers**

**Practical implications**

* Counts may be small; always present **absolute counts + %**.
* Use 3-year rolling averages if denominators <50.

**Bayesian estimation (technical)**

* Binomial(n, p), Prior: Beta(0.5,0.5).
* Posterior mean and 95% CrI.

---

**9. Disaggregation & Standardisation**

* By age and sex.
* **Age-standardisation:** WHO and ESP if comparing across populations.

---

**10. Importance / Uses**

* Supports quality improvement in lifestyle management.
* Identifies gaps in nutrition support services.

---

**11. Reporting Frequency & Format**

* Annual reporting.

---

**12. Interpretation Guidance**

* Low values highlight resource gaps or under-recording.

---

**13. Responsible Party**
Registry; dietetics service.

---

**14. Linkages to Other Metrics**

* Education (T2D-EDU-23)
* HbA1c control metrics (14–15).

---

**15. Metadata**

* Code: T2D-Diet-16
* Source: NICE QOF
* Version: 1.0

---

**16. Benchmark / Comparison Reference**

* **UK:** NHS QOF dietary review indicator.
* **International:** Limited — IDF guidelines for patient education.

**Bayesian estimation (technical)**

* Binomial(n, p), Prior: Beta(0.5,0.5).
* Posterior mean + 95% CrI.

---

**9. Disaggregation & Standardisation**

* By age and sex.

# 📑 Metric T2D-ACEARB-18: Percentage of patients with diabetes and nephropathy treated with an ACE inhibitor or ARB

**0. Priority**
**PRIMARY** — critical for renal protection, a major outcome of diabetes management.

---

**1. Definition (Official wording)**
NICE QOF: *Percentage of patients with diabetes and nephropathy (clinical proteinuria or microalbuminuria) currently treated with an ACE-I or ARB.*

---

**2. Plain Language Description**
Shows how many people with diabetic kidney disease are receiving the recommended protective medications.

---

**3. Formula**

* **% on ACE/ARB** = (Patients with nephropathy on ACE/ARB ÷ All diabetes patients with nephropathy) × 100

---

**4. Numerator & Denominator**

* **Numerator:** Patients with nephropathy receiving ACE/ARB therapy.
* **Denominator:** All diabetes patients with nephropathy.

---

**5. Variables Required**

* Diagnosis of nephropathy
* Medication record

---

**6. Data Source(s)**

* Registry
* Prescribing records

---

**7. Data Quality & Caveats**

* Requires reliable diagnosis coding.
* Treatment contraindications must be considered.

---

**8. Methodological Notes for Small Numbers**

**Practical implications**

* Numbers will be very small; report **absolute counts**.
* Suppress % if denominator <20.
* Pool data across years for stability.

**Bayesian estimation (technical)**

* Binomial(n, p), Prior: Beta(0.5,0.5).
* Posterior mean + 95% CrI.

---

**9. Disaggregation & Standardisation**

* By age and sex.
* **Age-standardisation:** WHO/ESP if comparing internationally, though small denominators limit use.

---

**10. Importance / Uses**

* Protects kidney function and reduces risk of end-stage renal disease.
* Monitors adherence to clinical guidelines.

---

**11. Reporting Frequency & Format**

* Annual, with multi-year pooling.

---

**12. Interpretation Guidance**

* Low coverage may reflect prescribing gaps or contraindications.

---

**13. Responsible Party**
Registry and primary care/renal services.

---

**14. Linkages to Other Metrics**

* BP control (T2D-BP metrics)
* Complication tracking

---

**15. Metadata**

* Code: T2D-ACEARB-18
* Source: NICE QOF
* Version: 1.0

---

**16. Benchmark / Comparison Reference**

* **UK:** NHS QOF nephropathy management indicator.
* **International:** KDIGO/IDF renal protection standards.

# 📑 Metric T2D-BP≤130/80-20: Percentage of people with type 2 diabetes with BP ≤130/80 mmHg

**0. Priority**
**PRIMARY** — blood pressure control is one of the strongest predictors of reduced cardiovascular risk.

---

**1. Definition (Official wording)**
IDF Clinical Guidelines Task Force: *Percentage of people with type 2 diabetes whose blood pressure is ≤130/80 mmHg.*

---

**2. Plain Language Description**
Shows the proportion of patients with diabetes who have well-controlled blood pressure.

---

**3. Formula**

* **% with controlled BP** = (Patients with last BP ≤130/80 ÷ All patients with type 2 diabetes) × 100

---

**4. Numerator & Denominator**

* **Numerator:** Patients with last BP ≤130/80.
* **Denominator:** All patients with type 2 diabetes.

---

**5. Variables Required**

* BP measurement
* Diabetes diagnosis

---

**6. Data Source(s)**

* Registry
* Clinical records

---

**7. Data Quality & Caveats**

* Based on latest BP reading, not average.
* Missing values may bias estimates.

---

**8. Methodological Notes for Small Numbers**

**Practical implications**

* Report **counts and %**.
* Suppress subgroup % if denominator <50.
* Use rolling averages for subgroup reporting.

**Bayesian estimation (technical)**

* Binomial(n, p), Beta(0.5,0.5).
* Posterior mean + 95% CrI.
* Trend smoothing possible with hierarchical models.

---

**9. Disaggregation & Standardisation**

* By age and sex.
* **Age-standardisation:** WHO and ESP for comparison.

---

**10. Importance / Uses**

* Strongly linked to reduced risk of stroke, kidney failure, and CVD.
* Critical for monitoring clinical quality.

---

**11. Reporting Frequency & Format**

* Annual.

---

**12. Interpretation Guidance**

* Higher % indicates better blood pressure control in the diabetes population.

---

**13. Responsible Party**
Registry; primary care and hypertension services.

---

**14. Linkages to Other Metrics**

# 📑 Metric T2D-MED-21: Diabetes medication use (none / tablets only / insulin only / combination)

**0. Priority**
**SECONDARY** — essential context for service planning and interpreting glycaemic control, but not itself an outcome or core burden metric.

---

**1. Definition (Official wording)**
CDC USDSS (adapted): *Distribution of current diabetes pharmacotherapy among people with diagnosed diabetes, categorised as: no medication; oral agents only; insulin only; insulin + oral combination.*

---

**2. Plain Language Description**
Shows how people with diabetes are being treated right now — with tablets, insulin, both, or no medication.

---

**3. Formula**

* **Share of category k (%)** = (Number of patients in category k ÷ All patients with diabetes) × 100
  *Categories:* none; tablets only; insulin only; combination.

---

**4. Numerator & Denominator**

* **Numerator:** Patients whose current treatment falls into category *k*.
* **Denominator:** All patients with diagnosed diabetes (or T2D if restricting to type 2).

---

**5. Variables Required**

* Diabetes diagnosis and type
* Current medication list (drug names, class, start/stop dates)
* Optional: contraindications/intolerance codes

---

**6. Data Source(s)**

* St Helena Diabetes Registry
* Prescribing/dispensing records (primary care pharmacy)

---

**7. Data Quality & Caveats**

* Medication lists must reflect **current** therapy (watch for stale repeats).
* Insulin “as needed” vs daily use should be distinguished where possible.
* Combination therapy must not double-count.

---

**8. Methodological Notes for Small Numbers**

**Practical implications**

* Always report **absolute counts and proportions** by category.
* Collapse rare cells (e.g., GLP-1 only) into “Other” to avoid suppressions.
* If any category count <5, aggregate with a neighbour (e.g., combine “insulin only” with “combination” for reporting).

**Bayesian estimation (technical)**

* Use **Dirichlet–Multinomial**: prior Dirichlet(α=0.5 for each category).
* Posterior Dirichlet(αk + xk) → report category means and 95% credible intervals.
* Optional partial pooling across years to stabilise trends.

---

**9. Disaggregation & Standardisation**

* Break down by **age group** and **sex** (no geography).
* **Age-standardisation:** If comparing internationally or to the UK, age-standardise category shares using the **WHO World Standard Population (2000–2025)** or **2013 European Standard Population (ESP)**.

---

**10. Importance / Uses**

* Informs procurement (insulin, strips, GLP-1s), workforce skills, and education needs.
* Contextualises HbA1c control metrics (different targets expected on insulin vs tablets).

---

**11. Reporting Frequency & Format**

* Annual snapshot; optional quarterly operational view.
* Stacked bar chart of category distribution; table with counts + %.

---

**12. Interpretation Guidance**

* Rising insulin share may reflect more severe disease or prescribing shifts.
* “No medication” can indicate early disease, lifestyle control, or care gaps — interpret with HbA1c.

---

**13. Responsible Party**
Registry manager; primary care pharmacy lead.

---

**14. Linkages to Other Metrics**

* HbA1c control (T2D-HbA1c<53-14; T2D-HbA1c≥75-15)
* SMBG among insulin-treated (T2D-SMBG-11)

---

**15. Metadata**

* Code: T2D-MED-21
* Source: CDC USDSS (adapted)
* Version: 1.0

---

**16. Benchmark / Comparison Reference**

* **UK:** NHS Digital, *National Diabetes Audit* (therapy profiles by age/sex).
* **International:** IDF Diabetes Atlas (treatment patterns, where available).

---

# 📑 Metric T2D-RET-22: Retinopathy exam within the last 12 months

**0. Priority**
**PRIMARY** — sight-saving process metric; a foundational quality standard for diabetes care.

---

**1. Definition (Official wording)**
NHS DESP / NDA (adapted): *Percentage of people with diabetes who received a retinal screening (dilated fundus photography or equivalent) within the last 12 months.*

---

**2. Plain Language Description**
Shows whether people with diabetes are getting their annual eye check to prevent vision loss.

---

**3. Formula**

* **% screened in last 12 months** = (People with diabetes with a retinopathy exam in past 12 months ÷ All people with diabetes eligible for screening) × 100

---

**4. Numerator & Denominator**

* **Numerator:** Eligible patients with a documented retinopathy screen in the last 12 months.
* **Denominator:** All patients eligible for screening (exclude medical exemptions, recent diagnosis if locally exempted, or those already under ophthalmology where screening is not indicated per pathway).

---

**5. Variables Required**

* Diabetes status and eligibility flag
* Date of last retinal screen; screening outcome (optional)
* Exemption/ophthalmology follow-up status

---

**6. Data Source(s)**

* St Helena Diabetes Registry
* Eye screening service / ophthalmology records

---

**7. Data Quality & Caveats**

* Ensure **eligibility** is correctly defined and recorded.
* Screens done off-island must be captured to avoid false “missed” screens.
* Distinguish screening from diagnostic ophthalmology visits.

---

**8. Methodological Notes for Small Numbers**

**Practical implications**

* Present **counts + %**; aim for **≥80–90%** coverage as a quality goal.
* If denominator <50 (e.g., age/sex subgroup), suppress subgroup %; use pooled multi-year.
* Consider **quarterly operational monitoring** to chase defaulters.

**Bayesian estimation (technical)**

* Binomial(n, p) with Jeffreys prior Beta(0.5,0.5).
* Posterior mean and 95% credible interval.
* Optional partial pooling across years or clinics.

---

**9. Disaggregation & Standardisation**

* By age and sex (no geography).
* **Age-standardisation:** For UK/global comparison, age-standardise coverage using **WHO World Standard Population** or **2013 ESP** (particularly if age structure differs).

---

**10. Importance / Uses**

* Early detection prevents sight loss.
* Core service quality metric; supports DESP-style assurance.

---

**11. Reporting Frequency & Format**

* Annual formal report; monthly/quarterly operational dashboards.
* Gauge chart vs target; trend line with 95% CrI.

---

**12. Interpretation Guidance**

* Low coverage often reflects **recall & reminder** issues, not capacity alone.
* Improving registry–screening linkage typically yields rapid gains.

---

**13. Responsible Party**
Registry manager; Eye Screening Service lead / Ophthalmology.

---

**14. Linkages to Other Metrics**

* HbA1c control (risk of retinopathy progression)
* Education uptake (T2D-EDU-23)

---

**15. Metadata**

* Code: T2D-RET-22
* Source: NHS DESP / NDA (adapted)
* Version: 1.0

---

**16. Benchmark / Comparison Reference**

* **UK:** NHS Diabetic Eye Screening Programme (DESP) and *National Diabetes Audit – Care Processes*.
* **International:** IDF and WHO eye health programme guidance.

---

# 📑 Metric T2D-EDU-23: Percentage of people with type 2 diabetes receiving formal diabetes education in the last year

**0. Priority**
**PRIMARY** — education underpins self-management, medication adherence, SMBG, diet, and risk reduction.

---

**1. Definition (Official wording)**
IDF (adapted to local context): *Percentage of people with type 2 diabetes who participated in a structured diabetes education programme within the last 12 months.*

---

**2. Plain Language Description**
Shows how many people attended a formal course or programme to learn how to manage their diabetes.

---

**3. Formula**

* **% receiving education** = (People with T2D who completed formal education in last 12 months ÷ All people with T2D) × 100

---

**4. Numerator & Denominator**

* **Numerator:** People with T2D with documented participation/completion of a recognised programme (e.g., group course, structured curriculum).
* **Denominator:** All people with T2D (or newly diagnosed subset, if running a “new diagnosis” metric variant).

---

**5. Variables Required**

* Diabetes type
* Education attendance/completion date and programme code
* Optional: delivery mode (group, one-to-one, digital), language, duration

---

**6. Data Source(s)**

* Registry (education module)
* Education provider records / sign-in sheets / LMS exports

---

**7. Data Quality & Caveats**

* Define “formal education” clearly (curriculum, duration threshold).
* Capture **completion**, not just referral or booking.
* Off-island or online completions must be recorded.

---

**8. Methodological Notes for Small Numbers**

**Practical implications**

* Report **counts + %**; if few completions, show trajectory over time.
* Suppress subgroup % if denominator <50; pool across years.
* Track **referral → attendance → completion** funnel in operational dashboards.

**Bayesian estimation (technical)**

* Binomial(n, p), Beta(0.5,0.5) prior.
* Posterior mean and 95% CrI; optional hierarchical pooling across cohorts/years.

---

**9. Disaggregation & Standardisation**

* By age and sex; optionally by **newly diagnosed vs established**.
* **Age-standardisation:** For UK/global comparison, age-standardise using **WHO World Standard Population** or **2013 ESP** where relevant.

---

**10. Importance / Uses**

* Strong evidence link to improved self-management and control.
* Identifies equity gaps (who isn’t getting access).

---

**11. Reporting Frequency & Format**

* Annual headline; quarterly operational tracking.
* Display funnel (referred → attended → completed) and overall completion % with 95% CrI.

---

**12. Interpretation Guidance**

* Low completion may reflect scheduling, transport, or cultural fit — pair with qualitative feedback.
* Digital or micro-modules can improve access in small islands.

---

**13. Responsible Party**
Registry manager; Diabetes Education Programme lead.

---

**14. Linkages to Other Metrics**

* SMBG (T2D-SMBG-11)
* HbA1c targets (T2D-HbA1c<53-14; T2D-HbA1c≥75-15)
* Retinopathy screening (T2D-RET-22)

---

**15. Metadata**

* Code: T2D-EDU-23
* Source: IDF (adapted)
* Version: 1.0

---

**16. Benchmark / Comparison Reference**

* **UK:** NHS Digital, *National Diabetes Audit – Structured Education* (e.g., DESMOND/DAFNE uptake, where available).
* **International:** IDF education standards and position statements.

---

## 📋 Minimal Core Dataset for Diabetes Registry

### 1. Demographics

* **Unique patient ID** (registry identifier, non-identifiable)
* **Date of birth** (→ derive age)
* **Sex**
* **Vital status** (alive/deceased; if deceased, date of death)
* **Population denominator source** (link to census/administrative data, not patient-level)

---

### 2. Diagnosis & Disease Status

* **Date of diabetes diagnosis**
* **Diabetes type** (Type 1, Type 2, Gestational, Secondary/Other)
* **Pregnancy status** (for women of reproductive age, yes/no at each encounter)
* **Pregnancy identifier** (episode-level ID, to link with maternal records)
* **Date of GDM diagnosis** (if applicable)
* **Nephropathy status** (none, microalbuminuria, proteinuria, other renal disease)

---

### 3. Laboratory & Clinical Measurements

* **HbA1c test date(s) + result(s)** (flag most recent result)
* **Blood pressure (systolic/diastolic, date measured)**
* **BMI** (useful for maternal and general risk stratification)

---

### 4. Medications

* **Current medication list** (drug name, class, start/stop date)

  * Flag: insulin (yes/no)
  * Flag: antihypertensive (yes/no)
  * Flag: ACE/ARB (yes/no)
* **Self-monitoring of blood glucose (SMBG) status** (yes/no; optional frequency)

---

### 5. Care Processes

* **Date of last dietary review**
* **Date of last retinal screening** (+ outcome if available)
* **Exemption/ophthalmology follow-up status** (yes/no)
* **Education programme attendance** (date, completion status)
* **Influenza vaccination status/date**

---

✅ With this **minimal dataset** we can:

* Calculate **all 23 metrics** directly or through derivation.
* Support **derived measures** like incidence, prevalence, age at diagnosis, and duration.
* Cover **process-of-care indicators** (HbA1c testing, diet, retinal exam, flu vaccine, education).
* Track **treatment and outcomes** (HbA1c thresholds, BP control, ACE/ARB use).

---

## 🔗 Crosswalk: Metrics ↔ Minimal Core Dataset

### 1. Incidence & Prevalence

* **T2D-INC-01 (Incidence)** → Date of diagnosis, Diabetes type, Age, Sex, Vital status, Population denominator
* **T2D-PREV-02 (Prevalence)** → Diabetes diagnosis status, Date of diagnosis, Vital status, Population denominator

### 2. Age & Duration

* **T2D-AGE-03 (Age at diagnosis)** → Date of birth, Date of diagnosis
* **T2D-DUR-04 (Duration)** → Date of diagnosis, Current date or Date of death

### 3. Maternal & Reproductive Health

* **T2D-PREG-05 (Diabetes in pregnancy)** → Pregnancy status, Diabetes type/status
* **T2D-GDM-06 (Gestational diabetes incidence)** → Pregnancy identifier, Date of GDM diagnosis, Maternal age, BMI
* **T2D-W18-44-07 (Women 18–44 prevalence)** → Age, Sex, Diagnosis status

### 4. Diabetes Type Distribution

* **T2D-TYPE-08 (Type distribution)** → Diabetes type

### 5. HbA1c Testing & Control

* **T2D-HBA1c-1x-09 (≥1 HbA1c in year)** → Diabetes type, HbA1c test date(s)
* **T2D-HBA1c-None-10 (No HbA1c in year)** → Diabetes type, HbA1c test date(s)
* **T2D-HbA1c≤64-12 (≤64 mmol/mol)** → Latest HbA1c result, Diabetes status
* **T2D-HbA1c≤75-13 (≤75 mmol/mol)** → Latest HbA1c result, Diabetes status
* **T2D-HbA1c<53-14 (<53 mmol/mol)** → Latest HbA1c result, Diabetes type
* **T2D-HbA1c≥75-15 (≥75 mmol/mol)** → Latest HbA1c result, Diabetes type

### 6. Other Clinical Management

* **T2D-SMBG-11 (Self-monitoring in insulin users)** → Diabetes type, Medication list (insulin flag), SMBG status
* **T2D-Diet-16 (Dietary review)** → Date of last dietary review, Diabetes diagnosis status
* **T2D-Flu-17 (Flu immunisation)** → Vaccination record, Diabetes diagnosis status
* **T2D-ACEARB-18 (ACE/ARB in nephropathy)** → Diagnosis of nephropathy, Medication record (ACE/ARB)
* **T2D-BP>140/90-19 (High BP untreated)** → Blood pressure, Medication status (antihypertensives)
* **T2D-BP≤130/80-20 (BP controlled)** → Blood pressure, Diabetes diagnosis status

### 7. Medication Profile

* **T2D-MED-21 (Medication use: none/tablets/insulin/combination)** → Current medication list, Diabetes type

### 8. Screening & Education

* **T2D-RET-22 (Retinopathy exam)** → Date of last retinal screen, Exemption/ophthalmology follow-up status, Diabetes diagnosis status
* **T2D-EDU-23 (Education uptake)** → Diabetes type, Education attendance/completion date

---

## ✅ Coverage Check

* **Demographics:** Needed for incidence, prevalence, reproductive health, and disaggregation.
* **Diagnosis & status:** Core to almost all metrics.
* **Labs & clinical measures:** Required for HbA1c, BP, nephropathy.
* **Medications:** Needed for SMBG, BP, ACE/ARB, therapy distribution.
* **Care processes:** Needed for diet, retinal screen, vaccination, education.
